title: Dynamic Tenancy Segmentation & Soft Capacity Failsafe PRD
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: This PRD defines a new Dedicated capacity feature set: dynamic tenancy segmentation plus a soft capacity failsafe (safety-net pool + soft-eviction + burst allocator). The goal is to reduce customer-facing unavailability during transient overloads while preserving per-tenant isolation and predictable unit economics.
goals: Reduce P99 latency and request drops for high-priority tenants during short-lived spikes
Introduce a small cluster-level safety-net pool to absorb transient bursts without overprovisioning tenant reservations
Implement soft-eviction scoring that prefers low-cost fallbacks and graceful degradation over hard preemption
Provide tenant segmentation controls that allow operators and customers to set isolation tiers and burst allowances
Expose telemetry and admin controls for tracing burst usage, soft-evictions, and safety-net consumption
non_goals: Replace existing hard-preemptive eviction mechanism for guaranteed contracts (we will fallback to existing behavior after failsafe thresholds)
Implement major scheduler rewrite — changes should sit above current scheduling kernels
Guarantee unlimited burst for all tenants; goal is controlled temporary relief not permanent overcommit
success_metrics: Reduction in tenant-facing 5xxs caused by capacity contention by >= 60% during spikes in pilot clusters
Decrease in customer-reported rollout incidents related to eviction by 50% for tenants in segment Tier-A
Safety-net pool absorbs at least 80% of transient spikes under 90s duration in synthetic benchmarks
No >2x increase in cost-per-token for served traffic using the failsafe compared to baseline
user_stories: As an SRE, I want a safety-net pool that automatically serves short bursts so customer SLAs stay intact during transient load
As a Platform PM, I want soft-eviction decisions to pick the least customer-impactful fallback (model variant, lower throughput) instead of immediate preemption
As a Dedicated tenant admin, I want to opt tenants into controlled burst allowances per billing period and see usage on the Console
As an on-call engineer, I want a clear alerting and runbook for when safety-net consumption exceeds threshold so I can escalate before SLA breaches
detailed_requirements: Safety-net pool: configurable percentage of cluster capacity (default 5%) reserved as transient capacity for short bursts; configurable per-cluster and per-region
Burst allocator: request-time decision service that checks tenant segment, recent burst history, and safety-net budget before granting burst capacity
Soft-eviction scoring: composite score using tenant priority, SLA tier, cost-sensitivity, recency of eviction, and fallback availability to choose victims
Tenant segmentation API: allow 3 segments by default (Isolated, Standard, Flexible) with tunable burst_percent and preemption_risk fields
Telemetry: expose per-tenant and per-cluster metrics for burst_grants, safety_net_consumed_seconds, soft_evictions_count, fallback_success_rate
Admin controls: emergency leash and manual reclaim button to drain safety-net pool and force revert to hard preemption
Accounting: map burst usage to billing metrics with clear tagging so Finance can report excess usage
Fallback chains: define ordered fallbacks per tenant (quantized model variant, reduced concurrency, slower batching) applied by soft-eviction before preemption
Config model: declarative JSON policy stored in control plane with validation, audit logging, and per-tenant overrides
api_changes: New control-plane endpoint: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/segmentation to change tenant segment and burst allowance
New read endpoint: GET /v1/clusters/{id}/safetynet to show pool size and current consumption
Billing tag change: include burst_grant_id on usage records for downstream aggregation
ui_changes: Console: per-tenant page shows 'Burst usage' card with historical consumption, bursts_remaining in billing period, and segment label
Console: cluster view shows safety-net utilization heatmap and alert status
Rollout toggle in Console Admin for enabling soft-eviction per cluster with a confidence slider
operational_changes: SLO updates: document expected behavior when safety-net is active and update SRE playbooks
Alerts: add alert when safety-net consumption > 75% for 5m and when soft-evictions > 10/min
Runbooks: expand on-call runbook to include steps for manual reclaim, customer communication template, and rollback to hard-preempt policy
Cost monitoring: new daily job to estimate cost delta introduced by safety-net usage for finance review
scope_changes: Initial scope limited to read-heavy, short-sequence workloads (seq_len <= 2048) to reduce kernel variation during pilot
No per-tenant autoscale policy changes in Phase 1 — autoscaler integration scoped to Phase 2
We will not expose per-request tenant opt-in via public API in Phase 1; only tenant-level controls in Console and control-plane API
acceptance_criteria: Pilot deployed to two dedicated clusters in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 with safety-net enabled
End-to-end burst allocator granted safety-net capacity for synthetic spike tests and traffic was served without 5xxs in >= 80% of trials
Soft-eviction logic selected at least one fallback chain instead of hard preemption for >= 90% of contention events during pilot
All new API endpoints have OpenAPI specs, integration tests, and RBAC checks documented
Console surfaces burst usage and safety-net status for tenants in pilot and admin reclaim operation succeeds in staging
Billing events containing burst_grant_id are emitted and validated against Finance queries
Security review completed and KMS audit logging applied to policy changes; security_review_required flag set to true
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (2 weeks): Implementation of safety-net pool and basic burst allocator; unit tests and local integration
Phase 1 (3 weeks): Deploy pilot to 2 clusters with 10 opt-in tenants; collect telemetry and iterate policy weights
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Expand to additional clusters, enable Console controls, and integrate billing tagging
Phase 3 (4 weeks): Gradual ramp to 25% of clusters with monitoring thresholds; freeze opt-in surface based on pilot success
Rollback plan: toggle off safety-net via control-plane and revert to hard-preempt scheduling; manual reclaim to drain pool
risks_mitigations: Risk: Safety-net can be drained by noisy tenants repeatedly — Mitigation: per-tenant burst budget and exponential backoff on grants
Risk: Cost blowup if safety-net serves long-lived traffic — Mitigation: limit maximum grant duration (default 90s) and monitor cost delta alerts
Risk: Incorrect soft-eviction scoring causes customer-facing regressions — Mitigation: conservative weights in pilot, simulated replays against historical contention traces
Risk: RBAC or API errors allow admin reclaim misuse — Mitigation: require two-step confirmation and audit logs for reclaim operations
notes: Keep Phase 1 conservative: default safety-net 5% and max grant duration 90s to limit cost exposure
We expect corner cases for model-variant fallbacks (compatibility and token accounting) — plan integration test matrix
Discuss potential legal/billing implications with Finance before enabling billing tags for production tenants
